summary: Sudoku helper package ships an opaque 34 MB Go binary as its Linux native component and executes it at postinstall, contradicting the shipped C source and README
details: @workoscalifant/sudoku-term ships a `prebuilt/linux-x64/sudoku-hint` file that is invoked automatically during `npm install` via a postinstall script that calls `execFileSync(bin, ['--selftest'],...)` on the platform-appropriate prebuilt binary. The README and the shipped `native/hint.c` describe this artifact as a ~26 KB statically-linked musl ELF compiled from a self-contained 200-line C sudoku solver with 'no files, no sockets'. The macOS prebuilt (~13 KB) is consistent with that description; the Linux prebuilt is a 33,976,468-byte Go executable containing Go runtime strings (`runtime.`, `GODEBUG`, `godebugs.Info`, `chacha8:`, `[bisect-`) and references to `/proc/self/cgroup` and `/proc/self/mountinfo`, and cannot be produced from the shipped C source. On Linux hosts, `npm install` therefore executes ~34 MB of author-controlled binary code whose behavior is not derivable from any source in the tarball, while the accompanying documentation and C source function as a cover story implying a small, transparent, network-free solver.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
